newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: No decision on unfreezing Iraqi assets for pilgrims.
newsitem.headline: No decision on unfreezing Iraqi assets for pilgrims.

text.p: The U.N. sanctions committee has not yet made a decision on a request by Baghdad for the release of $50 million in Iraqi frozen assets to enable Iraqi pilgrims to travel to Mecca this year, a committee source said on Monday.
The source denied a Baghdad report the United States and Britain, both members of the 15-nation committee, had blocked the request, though similar appeals in the past had been unsuccessful.
Iraq remains under stringent U.N. sanctions imposed since its 1990 invasion of Kuwait but the committee makes exceptions for humanitarian purposes.

The latest request asked for the release of $50 million from Iraqi assets frozen in Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates, as well as permission for Iraqi Airways planes to be allowed to carry pilgrims from Baghdad to Mecca.

The source said that, before the committee could make any decision, the countries holding the assets would have to say whether they were prepared to release some of the frozen Iraqi assets. Any unfrozen funds would have to be funnelled through a U.N. escrow account.
In the past the committee has always turned down requests for the use of Iraqi aircraft.
